comparisons.peer_topic: R&D Expense Increase and AI Headcount
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's research and development expenses increased by 10% to $6.5 billion in 2024, primarily driven by higher employee-related costs resulting from an increase in headcount to support the company's AI strategy.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD report increases in R&D expenses driven primarily by higher employee compensation and headcount growth. AVGO attributes its $4,057 million (77%) increase largely to the VMware Merger and higher grant-date fair values for equity awards. AMD reports a more modest 10% increase to $6.5 billion, citing higher employee-related costs due to headcount increases to support its AI strategy. While both identify compensation/headcount as the primary driver, AVGO's increase is significantly larger in absolute and percentage terms and explicitly links the volume of hiring to a specific merger event.

sentences.text: Research and development expense increased $4,057 million, or 77%, in fiscal year 2024, compared to the prior fiscal year.
The increase was primarily due to higher compensation, including higher stock-based compensation, as a result of an increase in headcount from the VMware Merger.
The increase in stock-based compensation expense was also due to annual employee equity awards granted at higher grant-date fair values.
Research and development expenses of $6.5 billion in 2024 increased by $584 million, or 10%, compared to $5.9 billion in 2023.
The increase was primarily due to higher employee-related costs due to an increase in headcount in support of our AI strategy.
